title: Gradient identities in simultaneous f-divergence dissipation
source_anchor: Sinho Chewi, Log-Concave Sampling, Theorem 8.3.1 proof: after differentiating q f(p/q), write rho=p/q and use grad p = rho grad q + q grad rho, grad(f'(rho)) = f''(rho) grad rho, and grad(f(rho)-rho f'(rho)) = -rho f''(rho) grad rho before the common-diffusion cancellation.
target_statement: Derive the three pointwise gradient identities used in Chewi Theorem 8.3.1 from Samplinglib's route-neutral HasGradientAt product and scalar-chain rules, including the scalar derivative identity d/dr[f(r)-r f'(r)] = -r f''(r).

searched: Libraries/shared-foundations.yml and active route:shared Frontier Cells
shared_floor_audit.notes: The general product/chain/quotient calculus is already canonical shared Samplinglib infrastructure and must be reused rather than duplicated. What is missing is the source-shaped adapter for Chewi 8.3.1, especially the complementary scalar derivative f-r f'. No current Riemannian/Optimisation consumer needs this exact f-divergence adapter, so the adapter remains route-local while its calculus parents stay shared.
